A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SPO and ExtendaBench study. All 18 pages of each version, including equations, tables, figures and appendices, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulation evaluations in VirtualHome and Habitat, component ablations, and additional vision-language model comparisons in Appendix B.

after.justification: v3 retains these original simulation results, ablations and appendix model comparisons.

M1.justification: The stated SPO loss in Eq. (6) changes from a preferred/rejected policy-probability ratio to a difference of policy/reference log-ratios. This is a limited correction to the reported objective. Scoring, preference selection and curriculum procedures remain unchanged; an implementation change is not established.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 1,509 ExtendaBench tasks: 605 in VirtualHome and 904 in Habitat 2.0, with the same four horizon categories and task scenarios.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 retain the same baseline, CoT, Self-Rewarding and Iterative RPO comparisons. Appendix Table 6 retains the same six vision-language models.

E3.justification: Sections 6.1, A.1.2 and B.1 retain the same reported splits, GCR/SR metrics, model configurations, sampling settings and training budgets. No new evaluation protocol is introduced.

E4.justification: Tables 3–4 retain the textual-coherence, image-awareness, curriculum and preference-selection ablations. Appendix word-frequency analyses and illustrated task examples are also unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run counts, seeds, uncertainty intervals or significance tests. The retained K=5 setting concerns candidate responses per prompt, not independent experimental runs.

E6.justification: All six tables, plotted data and qualitative findings are unchanged. For example, SPO's average GCR/SR remains 47.71%/16.83% in VirtualHome and 21.01%/15.36% in Habitat.

T1.justification: Equations (1) and (6) add reference-policy probability terms absent from v1's right-hand sides. This changes the mathematical loss specification beyond notation, but introduces no new theorem, proof or formal assumption.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions and performance claims concerning SPO, structured preference evaluation, curriculum training and ExtendaBench.

C2.justification: The interpretations of results and ablations are unchanged. The limitation concerning generalization from smaller to larger models moves verbatim from Appendix D to the main-text Limitations section.

D1.justification: v1 Appendix E specifies CC BY-NCSA 4.0 and noncommercial research use; v3 omits this disclosure. Hyperparameters, hardware and prompts in Appendices B–C remain unchanged. The omission does not establish that the actual dataset license changed.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion and bibliography are unchanged. The added Team (2025) citation in Section 6.2 identifies Qwen2.5-VL, already cited in v1's Table 6, without changing research positioning.

P1.justification: v3 expands two figure explanations, moves the limitations paragraph before the references, removes the license section, corrects 'WApplying' and updates an affiliation. The broader narrative and organization remain stable.

P2.justification: Figures 2–3 receive substantially fuller captions, and Figure 5 and appendix text reflow within the layout. The diagrams, plots, visual examples and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: Adding the missing reference-policy terms in Eqs. (1) and (6) improves the accuracy of the stated DPO formulation, while expanded captions clarify the method and data pipeline. These provide a limited net improvement despite the loss of dataset-license disclosure; the empirical evidence remains unchanged.
